optoSolverStatus.OPTIMAL: The best possible solution (globally optimal) to the defined problem
optoSolverStatus.FEASIBLE:
A feasible result indicates that the solution found is the best solution within a reasonable time limit,
but the optimizer was not able to prove it as the globally optimal solution. This is often the case when there are a large number of constraints involved
in the optimization case and it would be computationally heavy/time consuming for the optimizer to look for the globally optimal solution
optoSolverStatus.RELAXED: A relaxed solution means that one or multiple constraints of the original problem needed to be relaxed in order to find a solution
optoSolverStatus.SOLVER_ERROR:
The process was completed successfully, but there was no feasible solution with your bounds / constraints.
SOLVER_ERROR may be caused by missing data, bad case setup, or in rare cases, problem within the solver itself.
These statuses usually indicate software or model issues that require attention from support teams
optoSolverStatus.INFEASIBLE:
Infeasible results indicate that the optimizer could not find a solution within the given constraints.
The first step in rectifying this is to try to relax select constraints as the boundaries might be too tight for finding a solution
optoSolverStatus.INFEASIBLE_OR_UNBOUND:
UNBOUND may happen when there is leverage and, as a result, the optimal return may be infinite.
In other rare cases, the optimal return is actually finite, but it is so big (i.e. over 10,000%) that the optimizer believes the case is unbound.
In these cases, it is recommended to apply a constraint on the returns parameter
